title: Responsive design, UI/UX, and Tailwind
summary: Design mobile-first, choose content-driven breakpoints, create clear hierarchy, and translate the system into accessible Tailwind utilities.

lessons.title: Mobile-first and content-driven breakpoints
lessons.concept: Mobile-first defines the base layout for the most constrained space, then adds capabilities when content truly has room. A breakpoint responds to where composition breaks, not to a device name. Always separate the intention, the incoming data, the transformation being performed, and the observable result. This separation lets you predict behavior before running code and diagnose an error precisely.

explanation.title: Mental model
explanation.text: Mobile-first defines the base layout for the most constrained space, then adds capabilities when content truly has room. A breakpoint responds to where composition breaks, not to a device name. Always separate the intention, the incoming data, the transformation being performed, and the observable result. This separation lets you predict behavior before running code and diagnose an error precisely.

explanation.title: Simple analogy
explanation.text: Pack the essential cabin bag first, then add items only when a larger case becomes available.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply
explanation.text: Mobile-first defines the base layout for the most constrained space, then adds capabilities when content truly has room. A breakpoint responds to where composition breaks, not to a device name. Read the example from top to bottom, identify every input, and predict the output before running the command. This habit turns memorized syntax into reusable understanding.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply
explanation.text: Rules outside media queries apply everywhere; min-width progressively enhances them. rem units respect zoom, and continuous inspection from 320px upward reveals breakpoints. In a real project, verify this mechanism with the browser, terminal, or DevTools instead of assuming it works. Observable evidence is more reliable than intuition.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply
explanation.text: Start with one column, widen slowly, and add the second only when filters and content fit without compression. Also test long text, zoom, and landscape orientation. Finally apply the concept through one small isolated change, check the result, and revert if needed. Short changes make cause and effect easy to connect.

lessons.title: Visual hierarchy, rhythm, and feedback
lessons.concept: An interface guides attention through importance, proximity, contrast, and order. UX connects that reading to an understandable action, immediate feedback, and recovery after error. Always separate the intention, the incoming data, the transformation being performed, and the observable result. This separation lets you predict behavior before running code and diagnose an error precisely.

explanation.title: Mental model
explanation.text: An interface guides attention through importance, proximity, contrast, and order. UX connects that reading to an understandable action, immediate feedback, and recovery after error. Always separate the intention, the incoming data, the transformation being performed, and the observable result. This separation lets you predict behavior before running code and diagnose an error precisely.

explanation.title: Simple analogy
explanation.text: A shop window deliberately orders product, price, and action; if everything shouts, nothing guides.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply
explanation.text: An interface guides attention through importance, proximity, contrast, and order. UX connects that reading to an understandable action, immediate feedback, and recovery after error. Read the example from top to bottom, identify every input, and predict the output before running the command. This habit turns memorized syntax into reusable understanding.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply
explanation.text: A limited size and spacing scale creates predictable rhythm. Controls show hover, focus, pressed, loading, success, and error without abruptly shifting content. In a real project, verify this mechanism with the browser, terminal, or DevTools instead of assuming it works. Observable evidence is more reliable than intuition.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply
explanation.text: Provide one primary action per area, keep touch targets around 44px, and test by asking someone to verbalize what they would do next. Finally apply the concept through one small isolated change, check the result, and revert if needed. Short changes make cause and effect easy to connect.

explanation.title: hierarchy
explanation.text: Perceived order of importance.

explanation.title: affordance
explanation.text: Cue indicating how an element can be used.

explanation.title: feedback
explanation.text: Perceivable response to a user action.

explanation.title: General application
explanation.text: Prioritize goal, essential content, and action; remove visual accents that support no decision.

explanation.title: Application to L’ecomax
explanation.text: In ProductCard, image and name identify, price supports decision, shipping reassures, and one green button triggers purchase.

explanation.title: Expected result
explanation.text: Evidence of success: a user identifies product, price, and action within seconds, with a visible keyboard and touch target.

teaching.what: A responsive component protects its invariants—order, action target, stable media, variable content—in any container. It assumes neither a column count nor fixed data length. Always separate the intention, the incoming data, the transformation being performed, and the observable result. This separation lets you predict behavior before running code and diagnose an error precisely.
teaching.why: A responsive component protects its invariants—order, action target, stable media, variable content—in any container. It assumes neither a column count nor fixed data length. Read the example from top to bottom, identify every input, and predict the output before running the command. This habit turns memorized syntax into reusable understanding.

teaching.how:
aspect-square reserves media, grid rows pushes the action down, and h-full aligns a row of cards. motion-reduce disables nonessential transitions according to system preference. In a real project, verify this mechanism with the browser, terminal, or DevTools instead of assuming it works. Observable evidence is more reliable than intuition.
Test one- and six-line names, missing image, long price, 200% zoom, keyboard, reduced motion, and 160/280/420px containers. Fix the component rather than every host page. Finally apply the concept through one small isolated change, check the result, and revert if needed. Short changes make cause and effect easy to connect.
